transfers.source_mechanism: Mechanical deformation of a deformable matrix tunes the inter-element spacing of an ordered nanoreflector array, shifting the constructive interference condition to produce actively tunable narrowband reflection (color change).
transfers.target_problem:
LED Display Efficiency Improvement

Need: improve external quantum efficiency of micro-LED displays from 30% to 45%. Current losses: 40% total internal reflection at chip-epoxy interface, 15% absorption in substrate. Constraints: 1080p resolution, 1000 nits brightness, RGB color, 5-year lifetime. Must use existing GaN chip technology.
transfers.transferred_principle: Controlled mechanical strain applied to a deformable encapsulant layer containing an ordered nanostructure array shifts the periodicity of extraction features, optimizing the phase-matching condition for guided-mode outcoupling across the RGB spectrum to maximize broadband light extraction efficiency.
transfers.required_translation: Replace physiological actuation with manufacturing-stage mechanical strain (e.g., biaxial stretching of encapsulant film or pressure-assisted nanoimprint); replace iridophore nanoreflectors (guanine crystals) with high-index dielectric nanostructures (e.g., TiO2 nanorods or air-hole photonic crystal) embedded in UV-curable epoxy; replace color-tuning function with broadband extraction optimization targeting GaN guided modes; lock deformation via UV cure instead of continuous physiological control.
transfers.expected_effect: Reduces total internal reflection loss at chip-epoxy interface from 40% to <22% by providing optimized momentum-matching nanostructures for TE/TM guided modes across 450-630 nm, raising external quantum efficiency from 30% to >45% at 1000 nits while maintaining 1080p pixel definition and 5-year operational stability.
boundary_conditions: Encapsulant modulus must allow uniform deformation at <50°C before cure
Nanostructure aspect ratio >2 to survive strain without fracture
Strain uniformity <2% variation across 1080p panel (6.2M subpixels)
Refractive index contrast >0.5 between nanostructure and epoxy
Cure shrinkage <1% to preserve tuned periodicity
Thermal expansion mismatch <5 ppm/K between GaN and encapsulant
failure_conditions: Non-uniform strain causing >10% EQE variation between subpixels
Nanostructure collapse or coalescence during deformation
Epoxy modulus too high (>1 GPa pre-cure) preventing sufficient strain
Delamination at chip-epoxy interface under thermal cycling
Periodicity drift >5 nm post-cure due to stress relaxation
Absorption in nanostructure material >2% across RGB
transfers.testable_prediction: A 10 µm-pitch micro-LED with a biaxially strained (15% strain) TiO2-nanorod-epoxy encapsulant (periodicity tuned to 280 nm) will exhibit 47±2% EQE at 1000 nits across all RGB subpixels, with <3% efficiency drop after 1000 thermal cycles (-40°C to 85°C), compared to 32% EQE for an unstrained planar epoxy control.
